items.title: Derrick Gardner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 9, 2013
items.q: So the next day I got a call from Aaron Woodward, who was Count Basie’s adopted son. And he was in control of the orchestra as far as its bookings, and he owned the band basically. And he was in those meetings at Hampton. And so he called me and talked to me and kind of interviewed me on the phone I

ctx.x: What do you think, well some people talk about a significant big break or somebody took extra time with you and that caused a good shift for you. Was there a moment like that for you? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -4-

That would have to be the time when I joined the Basie band. As fate would have it, my mother got me the gig. Can you imagine that? My mother at the time was chairperson of the music department at Hampton University in Hampton, Virginia. And I was in grad school at Indiana University with Mike Woods. What happened was the Count Basie band was looking for a school to archive Basie’s stuff, music, other items, whatever, they were looking for a school. He chose Hampton. And with that they wanted to set up an annual…
I can see you calling the Registrar. That’s a good story. And were you basically sight reading, or you knew some of the music?
